text:
Maya: Quick sync - dedicated quota behavior: reserved throughput vs burst vs strict tenant isolation. Need concrete enforcement boundaries across gateway + runtime.

Kevin: Proposed split: gateway = fast token-bucket hints + short circuit 429s; runtime = authoritative admission + bounded tenant queues + hard rejects. Gateway should never promise more than runtime can deliver.

Sarah: Console requirement: single-row summary for each tenant: reserved_qps, reserved_used, burst_available, queued, isolation_mode. Inline toggle for Isolation (Shared / Strict) and a small cost impact preview.

Leo: Runtime admission pseudocode (high level):
```
quota = fetch_quota(tenant_id)
if running < quota.reserved_slots:
  admit
elif quota.burst_enabled and tenant_queue.size < quota.burst_limit:
  enqueue
elif running >= quota.hard_cap:
  reject(QUOTA_HARD_REJECT)
else:
  reject(QUOTA_DENIED)
```
Also: global safety check -> if cluster_util > 90% then force burst_enabled=false.

Nina: Telemetry needs: dedicated.tenant.reserved_used, dedicated.tenant.burst_used, dedicated.tenant.queue_depth, dedicated.tenant.rejects, dedicated.gateway_runtime_mismatch_count, plus queue_latency_p50/p95. Tag all metrics with tenant_id, cluster_id, region.

Kevin: Gateway algo: maintain per-key token bucket with refill = reserved_qps + soft_burst_tokens. soft_burst_tokens = floor(cluster_idle_capacity * tenant_burst_weight). Gateway attaches headers: X-Quota-Reserved, X-Quota-Burst-Remaining, Retry-After. Important: gateway may allow but runtime can still reject -> instrument that path.

Raj: Sales asks: enterprise customers will pay to disable bursting. Support isolation_mode: strict where reserved == hard cap and no burst or fallback. Also make hosted-fallback opt-in with policy flags (region/residency).

Diego: On provisioning: capacity planner must verify sum(reserved_qps) <= practical_cluster_capacity. If provisioning overcommits, allocation should fail or split into additional clusters. Runtime cannot mask provisioning mistakes.

OpsBot: deploy: quota-enforcer-v3 canary started at 2026-08-17T09:12:01Z :rocket:

Maya: Edge cases: KV cache warmups create spikes that look like burst. Options: (1) tag warmup requests and exclude from burst accounting, (2) maintain a small warmup bucket per tenant. Need to pick one.

Leo: Autoscaler note: scale target should be max(sum(reserved_qps), forecasted_99p_peak) + safety_margin. Use 5m hysteresis and limit scale rate (e.g., 2x per 10m) to avoid thrash. Also feed tenant_queue_depth as signal.

Nina: Alerts: tenant_reject_rate > 3% in 1m -> page oncall. gateway_runtime_mismatch_rate > 0.5% in 5m -> alert. global_burst_block_events spike -> ops warning and pause new canaries.

Sarah: UI export CSV columns: tenant_id, reserved_minutes_served, burst_minutes_served, minutes_queued, hosted_fallback_volume, estimated_cost_delta. Tooltip explains: "burst = temporary headroom beyond reserved; strict isolation disables burst."

Kevin: RFC schema example (will include full schema and validation rules):
```
tenant_quota:
  reserved_qps: 100
  burst_enabled: true
  burst_window_s: 60
  burst_limit: 300
  hard_cap: 1000
  burst_weight: 1.0
  isolation_mode: "shared" # or "strict"
  allow_hosted_fallback: false
```

Raj: I'll line up 2 pilots for strict isolation and 1 pilot for hosted-fallback measurement.

Maya: Action items: Kevin+Leo -> RFC with gateway + runtime flow + schema + migration story (EOD Friday). Nina -> telemetry + alert definitions. Sarah -> console mocks + export spec. Raj -> pilots.

Diego: One more: add a lightweight audit event when an admin flips isolation_mode for a tenant (who changed it, when, before/after), and surfacing that in tenant activity logs.

Maya: Good call. Also ensure fallback respects tenant.policy.data_residency.

Leo: I'll add warmup tagging and warmup_bucket suggestion to RFC and include sample admission pseudocode + metrics emitted on enqueue/dequeue/reject.

Maya: Okay if there are no blockers, start RFC. Post link back here when ready.

Sarah: :+1:

Nina: I'll draft alerts and metric dashboards for the canary.

Kevin: Will include examples of gateway headers and client-facing Retry-After semantics in RFC.

Maya: Closing thread; RFC link expected here once created.
